# CLAIMs with `tags` `philosophy-of-technology`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Philosophy of technology** — what technology is and what it does to those who live with it — the autonomy of technique, technological determinism and the social shaping of technology, lock-in and practical compulsion, automation and deskilling, technical codes and the politics of artifacts, design that steers or captures its users, critical theory of technology and convivial tools. A technology's regulation stays with society-and-governance, a measured effect of one product with social-science and a verdict on what is owed with ethics, unless the work argues about technology as such; how software is built is software-engineering (group: philosophy; ADR-098).

| [CLAIM-673](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-673.md) v2 | Where the capacities a collective needs to govern an arrangement are learned by exercise and lost with disuse, and the arrangement does the work through which they are exercised, the arrangement can erode the capacity to govern it, so that whether a collective can correct an arrangement is not independent of the arrangement | A's, from A8 §XVIII of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), "the deepest circularity within the theory": "A civilization needs wise and capable human beings to govern its technological systems, yet those technological systems help determine whether people develop the wisdom and capabilities necessary to govern them." The claim states the mechanism in the record's terms. If the capacities governing takes are kept by exercise, [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md)'s substitutive support applies to them, and the arrangement governed is the support. Interpretive: that governing capacities are of [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md)'s kind is the premise A assumes and the claim makes a condition. Filed on 2026-11-13 from the items the first filing left. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-674](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-674.md) | An arrangement, a technology among them, can satisfy people's preferences more fully, and raise the well-being they report, while narrowing their opportunities to engage actively with what is worthwhile, so success at satisfying preferences does not show that the lives an arrangement leaves open are going better | A's, from the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), A9 §III after the owner asked to "weave in susan wolf" (U7): "A society could become exceptionally good at identifying and satisfying people's preferences while simultaneously becoming worse at helping them encounter things worth caring about." A10 §V adds Sen's agency side: a deficiency "even if citizens report high levels of satisfaction". It rests on Wolf's account of meaning ([THEORY-1836](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1836.md)), applied to arrangements, which Wolf does not do ([ARG-106](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-106.md)). Marcuse's false needs ([THEORY-1853](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1853.md)) and Illich's needs that productivity cannot satisfy ([THEORY-1861](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1861.md)) corroborate it from other premises ([ARG-102](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-102.md)). The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md) v2 | Two forms of support that give a party the same capabilities now can leave it different capabilities later: where capacity is learned by doing and decays with disuse, support that does the work shrinks what the party can reach unaided while support that covers only its shortfall does not, so support, or a technology, cannot be ranked by present capability sets and has to be assessed by the capability trajectory it produces | A's, from the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13): A17 §V ("A technology can increase what someone accomplishes today while reducing what they will be capable of accomplishing tomorrow"; "We should investigate how particular forms of assistance change the person's future capability trajectory") and A23 §6 ("We therefore need to evaluate capability trajectories, not merely present capability sets"), joining [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md)'s capability trap to Sen's capability approach as [CLAIM-352](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-352.md) reads it. The derivation is checked here in [CLAIM-605](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-605.md)'s own model. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-676](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-676.md) | Two forms of assistance that deliver the same outcome can leave the person different participation in worthwhile activity, by removing drudgery, by opening an activity of worth to them, or by displacing participation they have reason to value, so assistance, a technology's above all, is assessed by the participation it enables or displaces as well as by its outcomes | A's, A9 §IV and §XI of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13): "The value of technological assistance should be assessed not only by the quality of the outcomes it produces, but also by the forms of human participation it enables or displaces", with three functions of automation, liberating, enabling and displacing. It complements [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md), which assesses support by the capability trajectory it leaves; this claim assesses it by the participation in worthwhile activity it leaves now. | [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md) v2 | A technology can become practically compulsory without any rule requiring it: as infrastructures, competitors and expectations adapt to its adoption, the alternatives left to those who decline it shrink, so the freedom an arrangement leaves is measured by what remains open to a non-adopter, not by what it lets adopters do | A's, from the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), stated four times: A3 §III ("collective dependence arising from individually rational behavior"), A8 §II's five stages, A11 §4 ("dependency lock-in") and A13 §II ("the dependency ratchet"). A technology adopted for a real advantage becomes a prerequisite for ordinary participation through three mechanisms that reinforce one another: infrastructure reorganizes around it, competition makes adoption "formally voluntary but strategically compelled", and expectations come to treat it as normal. A11 §4 gives the measure: "what possibilities remain available when they choose not to use it". The record holds lock-in among competing technologies ([THEORY-863](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-863.md)), in politics ([THEORY-885](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-885.md)) and of protective regimes ([CLAIM-445](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-445.md), [TERM-020](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-020.md)), and an arrangement that produces the dependence it exploits ([CLAIM-670](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-670.md)), but not the shrinking of the non-adopter's options or the measure. Illich's "radical monopoly", which A cites for it, is registered unread with Tools for Conviviality. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md) v4 | A dependence becomes presumptively dominating by those who control it when three conditions coincide: participation in an important sphere of life rests on the arrangement, those who control it hold consequential discretion over the dependent, and the dependent lacks effective means of protection, influence, challenge or justified withdrawal; this is a test for domination by an arrangement's controllers, not for every unfreedom, and impersonal constraint that no one holds is outside it | A's, from A13 §II of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13): a dependence is presumptively dominating by those who control it when essentiality, asymmetrical authority and inadequate accountability coincide. Narrowed at version 2, after the readings of 2026-11-13: version 1 said a dependence lacking a discretion-holder "is not domination, however complete"; Marcuse (through Farr), Han and Benjamin describe complete constraint with no one holding discretion, which some accounts call domination ([ARG-109](../../../record/arguments.d/ARG-109.md)). The claim is now a test for domination by an arrangement's controllers, not for every unfreedom. Zuboff 2022 is a worked case of all three conditions ([THEORY-1842](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1842.md)). Interpretive. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-684](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-684.md) v2 | When a choice about a technology or an institution could substantially and durably narrow the possibilities later open to those it affects, the burden of justifying it should rise with the size and the irreversibility of the narrowing | A's, A13 §VIII of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), "the reversibility principle", offered as "a practical formulation of restraint": "When a technological choice could substantially and durably narrow future human possibilities, the burden of justification should rise with the magnitude and irreversibility of the change." It answers the ratchet A described ([CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md)) with a rule for deciding before lock-in, and A pairs it with pilots, independent evaluation and appeals. Interpretive. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [CLAIM-688](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-688.md) v2 | A collective's capacity to decline a feasible technology, which is part of its self-direction over that technology, can depend more on the competition it is in than on its own organization: where forgoing the technology leaves a collective dependent on rivals that adopt it, none of the competitors can decline it alone, and the capacity exists, if anywhere, in coordination among them | A's, from the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13). A8 §XV and A13 §X make restraint a form of agency: "the capacity to decide against exercising a capability when doing so would undermine more important goods", so that a civilization unable to choose against a feasible development "possesses enormous instrumental power but limited collective self-direction". A8 §IX, A11 §29 and A13 §XI then give "the competitive necessity problem": a society that restrains itself "could become increasingly dependent" on societies that do not. Put together, the claim places the capacity to decline in the competition, not in the collective. [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md)'s competitive mechanism is the same thing one scale down, for a person among firms or peers; [CLAIM-457](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-457.md) says coordinated parties can do what none can alone, which is A's first response. Interpretive. Filed on 2026-11-13 from the items the first filing left. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
